1. Model consistently underestimates true prices, especially in the first 10–15 days of the forecast horizon — adjust upward by 5–15% for early periods.  
2. After sharp price spikes (e.g., >40%), model overreacts and overshoots — reduce forecast by 3–8% in the following 3–5 days.  
3. Model exhibits mean reversion bias — if 3–5 consecutive days show downward drift, forecast should not continue falling; expect rebound within 7–10 days.  
4. Forecast horizon 30d is prone to lag — if true outcome shows strong upward trend, model lags by 2–4 days; adjust forecast to align with 3–5 day lag.  
5. Model fails to capture seasonal or event-driven surges — if history includes high volatility or policy changes, increase forecast sensitivity by 10–20% for next 5–7 days.
